title: Qualification Criteria for Entry to Each Corporate Travel Programme
content:
A company qualifies for a tier of the Corporate Travel Programmes on three criteria published for that tier: the seats it contracts for, the annual booking value it brings, and whether the tier is reached only through a formal tender.

| Programme tier | Seats contracted, at least | Annual booking value, at least | Formal tender required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Business Starter Programme | 1 | 0.00 USD | No |
| Business Team Programme | 5 | 50000.00 USD | No |
| Business Pro Programme | 20 | 250000.00 USD | No |
| Business Enterprise Programme | 75 | 1000000.00 USD | No |
| Business Enterprise Plus Programme | 250 | 4000000.00 USD | Yes |
| Business Global Programme | 750 | 12000000.00 USD | Yes |

## Notes to the criteria

1. Each seat figure and each value figure is a floor, read inclusively: a company contracting exactly 20 seats and bringing exactly 250000.00 USD of annual booking value meets both criteria published for the Business Pro Programme.
2. The Business Starter Programme publishes no booking value criterion, its figure standing at 0.00 USD, and asks for 1 seat.
3. The seat floors run 1, 5, 20, 75, 250 and 750 across the six tiers; the annual booking value floors run 0.00 USD, 50000.00 USD, 250000.00 USD, 1000000.00 USD, 4000000.00 USD and 12000000.00 USD.
4. A formal tender is published as required for the Business Enterprise Plus Programme and the Business Global Programme. The four tiers below them are not published with a tender requirement.

## Points of judgement

**A company contracting 60 seats with 300000.00 USD of annual booking value.** It meets the 20 seats and 250000.00 USD published for the Business Pro Programme. It does not meet the 75 seats published for the Business Enterprise Programme.

**A company bringing 5000000.00 USD of annual booking value and contracting 300 seats.** It meets the 250 seats and 4000000.00 USD published for the Business Enterprise Plus Programme, a tier published as reached through a formal tender.
